study type: Diagnostic accuracy study with retrospective analysis
cohort: The study included 230 female infants, predominantly under 3 months of age, comprising a healthy control group, infants with anteriorly displaced anus (ADA), infants with anorectal malformation (ARM), and infants with vestibular anus.
finding: A urethra-to-anus distance (UAD) of less than 17 mm on perineal ultrasound appears to be a crucial cut-off for identifying anteriorly displaced anus associated with anorectal malformations.
cross-section timing: Primarily under 3 months of age, with some follow-up beyond 3 months for ADA patients.
